title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming + function/tool calls + structured output
author: Alex Kim
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer into parity with /v1/chat.completions for feature coverage required by product teams and partners. This PR expands support for: explicit message roles (system/user/assistant), stop sequences and logprobs passthrough, streaming stability for chunked tool/function call sequences, and structured output formatting compatibility (content filters and JSON-like tool responses). It also fixes streaming edge-cases where function call fragments and final JSON objects could be split across chunks and cause downstream parsers to fail.

What this changes: single continuous compatibility handler that maps Redwood RPC to OpenAI-style chat parameters; improved streaming buffer/assembler that preserves chunk boundaries for function/tool calls and emits well-formed events; new `logprobs` passthrough where available (model dependent), canonical handling of `stop` sequences, and response-formatting hooks so customers using structured output receive identical shape to the OpenAI endpoint.

Compatibility notes: default behavior is backward-compatible. Customers using Redwood-native endpoints see no change unless they opt-in to the OpenAI compatibility shim. All OpenAI-specific parameters are opt-in via the compatibility flag `openai_mode=true` on the route config. When enabled, we intentionally mimic OpenAI semantics (e.g., role normalization, stop truncation rules). Edge behavior (truncation/stop precedence) follows the OpenAI documented priority; tests added to lock semantics.

Testing and validation: extensive unit and integration tests added for streaming assembly, function/tool call boundaries, and structured JSON emission. E2E smoke harness run against several curated models (including quantized variants) to validate latency/regressions. Perf benchmarks show <5% median token latency impact and improved streaming tail stability.

Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated with 1% of traffic for 24h, then 10% for 48h, monitor structured-output regressions and TB failure rate. Feature gated behind `openai_compat` flag for private deployments.

Files of interest and a brief rationale are included below. See release_notes for user-facing notes and migration guidance.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add chat.completions parameter mapping, role normalization, and stop handling
fix(streaming): stabilise chunk assembly for function/tool call payloads and prevent split-JSON emits
test(openai-compat): add integration tests for stop/logprobs, streaming tool calls, and structured output
docs(openai): document openai_mode flag, param differences, and migration guidance
perf(streaming): micro-optimise buffer allocation and avoid copies during assembly
review_comments: Priya Patel: Overall looks good. Please add explicit tests for multiple simultaneous stop sequences and document expected precedence. (addressed in tests/integration/openai_chat_parity.rs)
Miguel Santos: Streaming assembler looks correct, but please add a comment on the concurrency model in stream_assembler.rs — clarified inline and added an assert to avoid concurrent mutation.
Dana Lee: We should ensure the openai_mode flag cannot be toggled mid-request on Dedicated; added validation in chat_endpoint.rs and unit tests to prevent runtime flips.

Alex Kim (author): Responded: added tests, inline docs, and validation. Fixed the edge-case where logprobs slices were empty for certain model backends by normalizing to null. CI re-run to validate integration tests.
Priya Patel: Approved after the integration test fixes and the canary rollout plan update.
ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky->pass (initial failure on stream assembly; fixed by stronger buffer handling)
e2e-smoke: pass (smoke harness against two curated models)
perf-bench: pass (median token latency +4.1%, p95 +6% on canary workloads)
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility mode: role normalization (system/user/assistant), stop sequence behavior consistent with OpenAI, opt-in logprobs passthrough where supported by model, improved streaming stability for function/tool calls and structured output parity. Enabled behind 'openai_mode' flag. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration steps and examples.
notes_for_cherry_pick: Backport to release/2026-02 required for Dedicated customers requesting early opt-in. Cherry-pick excludes perf micro-opts that require kernel changes (see perf commit comments).
user_impact: Low by default (opt-in). Customers enabling openai_mode may see small latency increase; streaming stability fixes improve parser reliability for tool-function integrations.
qa_summary: QA covered: unit tests, integration tests simulating partial stream fragments, end-to-end smoke tests, and a 48h canary on staging. Regression threshold alerts added to SLO dashboards.
migration_guidance: Enable openai_mode on a per-route basis. For Private installations, ensure operator sets openai_compat: true in the route config and runs a short canary before broad rollout. If you rely on Redwood-native structured outputs, no change unless openai_mode is enabled.
changelog_entry: 2026-03-03: OpenAI chat.completions compatibility mode (roles, stop/logprobs, streaming function/tool parity, structured output) - opt-in behind openai_mode flag.
